content.summary_of_the_paper:
Summary of the paper
The authors study a variant of the protein interaction prediction problems when more than two proteins are involved. Prior work such as the  EquiDock (Ganea et al.) was designed for binary interaction between two proteins.

A neural architecture called xTrimoDock based on attention layers was designed to combine information from sequence and structure modalities with pooling layers to predict 3D frames of proteins. The training is multi-steps, meaning that the predicted 3D frames are fed back to the network to update the predicted frames.

The authors performed experiments on the standard benchmark datasets using the Database of Interacting Protein Structures (DIPS) as training and validation data, while the test set consists of 27 antibody-antigen complexes released after October 2021 that have not been used to train AlphaFold-Multimer for a fair comparison.

Baselines chosen for comparison included four docking software ZDOCK (Chen et al. (2003)), HADDOCK (De Vries et al. (2010)), ClusPro (Kozakov et al. (2017)), HDOCK (Yan et al. (2020)), two deep learning models EquiDock (Ganea et al. (2022)) and AlphaFold-Multimer (Multimer for short, Evans et al. (2021)). 

Among those, only AlphaFold-Multimer was designed for 3 or more protein interaction predictions, while all other baselines were designed for binary prediction.

In terms of demonstrated results, Table 2 shows that significant reduction in prediction error measured as the RMSD metrics compared to standard binary interaction prediction methods and AlphaFold-Multimer.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths

This a well-written paper.

Significant experimental results.

Interesting multi-step learning methods.

Weaknesses

The reported results were on multi-chains with at least 3 chains. To demonstrate the significance of the proposed architecture compared to existing methods, additional experiments are needed on test data with only binary interaction. It is unclear from the paper whether the given proposed approach is only better than existing approaches on multi-chains with at least 3 chains test cases.

The method for adaption of baseline models trained for prediction of binary interaction to the multi-chains prediction problems with at least 3 chains was not described in the paper. I think different ways of casting the binary interaction prediction into multi-chain interaction prediction will lead to very different results and thus need to discuss carefully in the paper.

In general, the methods designed for binary interaction prediction like EquiDock or other docking baselines based on simulation can be extended for multi-chain interaction problems. To demonstrate that the proposed method xTrimoDock has special ingredients that make it deal with multi-chain prediction problems better than those extensions, I would expect to see more technical depths on the difference between binary and multi-chain cases. In the current design, I see that the significance of the results mainly comes from the fact that xTrimoDock was trained with multi-chain prediction data while other models like EquiDock were trained with binary prediction and adapted to the multi-chain prediction case.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Originality and clarity
The paper was well written, yet its novelty is limited. A minor change to the existing methods to cope with a new variant of the protein prediction problem.

The paper provided details about experimental settings but the source code was not included or open-sourced so reproducibility is questionable.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper was well-written, but I don't see the significance of technical contribution compared to existing related arts. Even the experimental results were significant but it comes from the fact that xTrimoDock was trained with multi-chain prediction data while other models like EquiDock were trained with binary prediction and adapted to the multi-chain prediction case. The adaptation from binary prediction to multi-chain cases was not clearly described in the paper.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper studies the task of rigid protein-protein docking task under the more ubiquitous multi-chain complex setting. The authors propose a novel model called xTrimoDock for this task, which consists of a cross-modal transformer to integrate representations from protein sequences and structures, and a multi-step prediction of rotations and translations to accomplish the multi-chain docking. Comprehensive experiments have been conducted and validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in terms of both effectiveness and efficiency.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

- The proposed frame is novel and the two key components (namely the cross-modal transformer and multi-step prediction) are intuitive and sound.
- The experiments are comprehensive, and the result can prove the superior performance the proposed approach in terms of both effectiveness and efficiency.
- In the task of complex prediction, significant performance improvements can be observed by using the proposed .

Weaknesses:

- The task definition is not clear for the general readers in computer science. The authors should formal define the task, as most of the data input are obtained from third party models, which is not intuitive for readers to understand the input and its challenging of the task.
-  A more detailed ablation study over the different loss components is preferred.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors of this paper present a Transformer-based model named xTrimoDock for multi-chain protein docking. This model has two major components: (1) two-modal Transformer that considers both sequence and structure information, and (2) multi-step prediction that fine-tune the prediction using the same Transformer. Experimental results show that xTrimoDock performs better than existing methods for multi-chain protein docking.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. Different from existing work which deals with binary chain docking, this paper focuses on multi-chain docking. Experimental results show that the performance of xTrimoDock is generally better than binary-chain docking methods.   

Weaknesses:
1. Back-bone frames and chain-level frames are used in the model. The authors should explain what "frame" exactly mean. This concept was taken from previous work, but its definition should be discussed in the paper so that readers do not need to read related work. 
2. Since this paper concentrates on multi-chain docking, the performance should be investigated in terms of number of chains (i.e, 2, 3, 4,...).  
3. The presentation of this paper could be further improved by fixing some minors, for example capitalization issues in the main text and references.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The contributions of this paper is clearly demonstrated. The novelty of this resides in the dual-modal Transformer and multi-step refinement of the prediction for multi-chain protein docking. If source code is provided in the final version, there shouldn't be major issues to reproduce the results.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I think it is a good paper in protein docking. There are a mediate dose of novelty in the model and the experimental results are very positive. For improvement, I would like to see changes of performance with the increase of chain number.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
